newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Moslem rebels willing to resume talks with Manila.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels willing to resume talks with Manila.

text.p: Moslem rebels in southern Philippines are willing to resume peace negotiations with Manila as soon as fighting dies down, former guerrilla chief Nur Misuari said on Friday.
"Returning to the negotiating table is not a problem to the MILF (Moro Islamic Liberation Front) once the situation is normalised," Misuari said in a report to the presidential palace.
Misuari met MILF vice chairman Hadji Murad on Wednesday upon instructions from President Fidel Ramos to persuade his former allies to resume peace talks.
MILF called off scheduled peace talks last month after a series of clashes with government forces which culminated in the capture of an MILF base in Maguindanao province.
Misuari, chief of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), headed the largest guerrilla group in Mindanao ntil he signed a peace deal with the government last September.
He is now the governor of a semi-autonomous Moslem area.
The MILF, with an estimated 6,000 fighters, is a breakaway guerrilla faction still fighting for an Islamic state.
On Thursday, the Philippine army extended by four days a unilateral ceasefire.
